title: The Evening Brief: A day of dugout and depth-chart resets, one credential at a time
dek: The Angels replaced their entire pitching coaching staff, the Browns named Deshaun Watson their preseason starter, and a former FIFA Council member's break with Infantino kept drawing coverage, while injury updates on Bardghji, Greenard, and Stiggers remained open.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The day's throughline is institutions and rosters absorbing pressure in real time, from a last-place coaching staff to a fractured FIFA coalition, with several individual outcomes still unresolved.
bottom_line: The day's clearest development was the Browns naming Deshaun Watson their preseason opener starter against Chicago, his first game since an October 2024 Achilles tear, alongside the Angels' wholesale dismissal of their pitching coaching staff at 45-74. Injury situations involving Stiggers, Greenard, and Bardghji remained open without confirmed diagnoses or return timelines, and the FIFA story advanced as Isha Johansen's public call for Infantino's resignation continued to draw reaction without a response yet from CAF. The honest read is that most threads from today, the transfer talks, the injury outlooks, and the FIFA dissent, are still unresolved in the reporting. Checkpoints ahead include Saturday's Browns-Bears preseason game, the September 1 transfer deadline, and any further African football response to Johansen's statement.
body: The clearest new fact of the evening is the Browns naming Deshaun Watson their starting quarterback for Saturday's preseason opener against Chicago, his first game action since tearing his right Achilles in October 2024 and undergoing a second surgery in January 2025. Shedeur Sanders will start the second preseason game against Buffalo on August 22, continuing the quarterback competition that has had the two alternating first-team reps in practice.

Elsewhere, the day's stories continue to cluster around organizations and figures under strain rather than around game results. The Angels fired pitching coach Mike Maddux and assistants Darryl Scott and Dom Chiti, naming Tim Leveque and Michael Wuertz as interim replacements, with the team at 45-74, the worst record in the majors, and a pitching staff that leads MLB in walks. Manchester City completed a two-year deal for goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille as backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma, while Inter Milan remained in advanced but unfinished talks with Tottenham for full-back Djed Spence, a deal reported at a minimum of 25.6 million pounds.

The FIFA story kept developing through the day: Isha Johansen, a former FIFA Council member and ex-Sierra Leone FA president, publicly called on Gianni Infantino to resign over the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, becoming the first prominent African football figure to break from the continental bloc that has backed him. CAF's executive committee has unanimously supported Infantino's 2027 re-election, and the reporting does not yet say whether other African officials will follow Johansen or how CAF plans to respond.

On the injury front, several threads opened earlier in the day remain open tonight. Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers collapsed during a joint practice with Tampa Bay and was hospitalized; coach Aaron Glenn said he was conscious and able to speak, but no diagnosis has been reported. Eagles pass rusher Jonathan Greenard will miss at least another couple of weeks with a pectoral strain, and defensive coordinator Vic Fangio would not commit to him practicing before the regular season. Barcelona's Roony Bardghji tore the ACL in his right knee in training, the second tear to that same knee in two years, ruling him out of any summer transfer before the September 1 deadline. None of these three situations has a confirmed return timeline in tonight's reporting.

The why behind these stories varies by story. The Angels' coaching change is explicitly tied to a historically bad record and a walks problem the reporting quantifies. The FIFA dissent is tied to the specifics of the Forward Enterprise proposal and Infantino's own past advice to Johansen, which she is now turning back on him. The injuries to Stiggers, Greenard, and Bardghji are reported as medical events with outcomes the stories do not yet know, and none of the reporting speculates beyond the official statements given.

Separately, Matt Hasselbeck's participation in a Boston University study seeking the first living diagnosis of CTE continued to draw coverage, underscoring that the research is early stage, multi-site, and funded by a $15 million NIH award, with no timeline yet for a usable diagnostic tool. HISA's investigation into five races at Saratoga and Monmouth Park, involving horses linked to one Maryland training facility and unusual betting patterns flagged by U.S. and U.K. bookmakers, also remains open, with no findings released.

What to watch in the coming days: Watson's performance Saturday against Chicago and whether Monken's quarterback decision crystallizes after the Bills preseason game on August 22; updates on Bardghji's surgery and recovery timeline; Greenard's practice status ahead of Week 1; further word on Stiggers's hospital evaluation; whether the Spence-Inter deal is finalized before September 1; any HISA findings from the five flagged races; and whether other African football officials follow Johansen's public break with Infantino.
